subject: Architecture
title: Supertall Sustainability: Green Giants
description: One-minute skill: Supertall Sustainability: Green Giants.

hook.text: Skyscrapers guzzle energy. But the newest ones are fighting back with radical green design.

buildup.text: Shanghai Tower spirals to reduce wind load by 24 percent, cutting the steel needed by thousands of tons.

discovery.text: Double-skin facades trap air between glass layers, acting as insulation that slashes heating costs.

twist.text: Some supertalls now generate more energy than they use, with built-in turbines and solar glass.

climax.text: Singapore's CapitaSpring has four stories of sky gardens inside the tower, growing food for tenants.

punchline.text: The tallest buildings are learning to be the greenest ones too.

quiz.question: How does Shanghai Tower's spiral shape help sustainability?
options: It reduces wind load, cutting steel requirements
It allows more natural sunlight into every floor
